note: The mapping identifies the OSCAL models used by seven parties from guidance publication through audit. Component types distinguish guidance from checks where both use component definitions. Two groups identify guidance authors and automation providers and operators. Policy engine providers build tools; system owners and auditors execute the flows shown. Mapping providers are separate because guidance authors do not always publish framework mappings: STIGs carry CCIs, DISA's CCI list names the 800-53 controls, and third parties publish mappings through NIST's OLIR programme.
intro: Seven parties publish, implement or assess hardening guidance. The table maps each party to OSCAL models and groups guidance authors separately from automation providers and operators.

parties.name: Regulatory control providers
parties.who: NIST and other bodies publishing regulatory controls, such as SP 800-53

parties.name: Mapping providers
parties.who: Organisations linking guidance to frameworks through DISA's CCI list, NIST's OLIR programme or the Secure Controls Framework

parties.name: Technical hardening guidance providers
parties.who: CIS, DISA and other benchmark publishers

parties.name: Technology providers
parties.who: Vendors publishing configuration guidance for hardware, software and services, independently or with benchmark publishers such as CIS

parties.name: Policy engine providers
parties.who: Providers of assessment and checking tools such as OPA, Kyverno, ScubaGear and OpenSCAP

parties.name: System owners
parties.who: Organisations implementing and documenting controls on a system

parties.name: Independent auditors
parties.who: Assessors running checks and reviewing results independently of system owners

mapper.note: The mapping provider writes a separate framework mapping. The published corpus contains no mapping collection for hardening guidance.

engine.note: The provider publishes checks as components of type software, referencing the guidance authors' catalog. System owners and auditors run the checks.

owner.note: The system owner selects requirements and merges catalogs through a profile imported by the system security plan.

auditor.note: The auditor runs the checks independently. The resulting finding targets the system owner's implementation statement.

mapper.note: The mapping provider edits a component definition. Whether the rules or the checks carry the framework mapping remains open.

engine.note: The provider publishes checks in a component of type validation. System owners and auditors run the checks.

auditor.note: The auditor runs checks through an assessment plan, allowing the result to identify a host rather than a component.

mapper.note: The mapping provider edits the assessment plan, naming the framework controls covered by the activity.

benchmark.note: The guidance provider writes activities and steps. The policy engine provider supplies executable checks.

software.note: The technology provider writes activities and steps. The policy engine provider supplies executable checks.

engine.note: The policy engine provider adds checks to the assessment plan. The plan identifies the engine in assessment-assets.

owner.note: The system owner supplies the profile and system security plan. The assessor's workflow does not depend on the owner's automation.

auditor.note: The auditor's run produces assessment results, not implementation claims. The workflow does not update the system security plan.

groups.label: Hardening guidance authors
groups.note: Benchmark publishers and technology providers author guidance in the same OSCAL model for each approach.

groups.label: Automation providers and operators
groups.note: Providers build policy engines. System owners and auditors run checks to produce implementation responses or assessment results.

runtime: A policy engine reads OSCAL, executes checks and writes OSCAL. Providers publish the checks; each flow identifies the party executing the checks.
